origin: computed by us from RTOFS, with TEOS-10
definition: RTOFS Tropical Cyclone Heat Potential at the profile position: heat above the 26 C isotherm.
computation: Daily field: TCHP = 1e-7 * sum over HYCOM layers above D26 of rho * cp * max(T - 26, 0) * dz_eff, with p = gsw.p_from_z(-z, lat), SA = gsw.SA_from_SP(S, p, lon, lat), rho = gsw.rho_t_exact(SA, T, p) and cp = gsw.cp_t_exact(SA, T, p) (TEOS-10), layer thickness = HYCOM thickness (Pa) / 9806, dz_eff the full layer if it lies above D26 or the part above D26 if it straddles it. Source: rtofs_glo.t00z.f06.archv (00Z cycle, 6-h forecast). Then sampled to the Argo position by inverse-distance-squared weighting over the 8 nearest RTOFS grid cells: F = sum(w_i F_i) / sum(w_i), w_i = 1/d_i^2, missing neighbours excluded. NaN where the column never reaches 26 C.
upstream: RTOFS does not publish TCHP. We compute it from the RTOFS 3D fields `temp`, `salin` and `thknss` in rtofs_glo.t00z.f06.archv.a/.b; the formula is the Leipper & Volgenau (1972) definition, with density and heat capacity from TEOS-10. RTOFS temperature is potential temperature but is used as in-situ temperature here; see [Known approximation](#known-approximation-potential-vs-in-situ-temperature).

origin: computed by us from RTOFS, no TEOS-10
definition: RTOFS depth of the 26 C isotherm at the profile position.
computation: Daily field: first HYCOM layer (from the surface) with T <= 26 C, linearly interpolated between that layer's centre depth and the one above: D26 = z1 + (T1 - 26)/(T1 - T2) * (z2 - z1). Requires the top layer to be >= 26 C. Then sampled to the Argo position by inverse-distance-squared weighting over the 8 nearest RTOFS grid cells: F = sum(w_i F_i) / sum(w_i), w_i = 1/d_i^2, missing neighbours excluded.
upstream: RTOFS does not publish D26. We compute it from the RTOFS 3D fields `temp` and `thknss`; no TEOS-10 is involved (depth = layer pressure thickness / 9806 Pa per m). RTOFS temperature is potential temperature but is used as in-situ temperature here; see [Known approximation](#known-approximation-potential-vs-in-situ-temperature).

origin: derived by us from RTOFS values

origin: derived by us from RTOFS values
definition: Standard deviation of RTOFS TCHP within about 1 degree of the profile.
computation: Population std (ddof=0) of valid cells, h = 12 cells (~2 x 2 degree box); from the daily RTOFS field at the nearest grid cell (y0, x0); square window |y - y0| <= h, |x - x0| <= h cells on the native 1/12-degree grid (longitude wraps); valid (finite) cells only, and NaN unless valid cells cover >= 25% of the window.

origin: derived by us from RTOFS values
definition: Magnitude of the horizontal gradient of RTOFS TCHP.
computation: 100 * sqrt(((F[y0,x0+1] - F[y0,x0-1]) / (2 dx))^2 + ((F[y0+1,x0] - F[y0-1,x0]) / (2 dy))^2), centred differences at the nearest grid cell, dx and dy the local grid spacings in km (dx shrinks with cos lat). NaN if any of the four neighbours is missing.
upstream: Statistic of our daily RTOFS TCHP field (see model_interp_tchp_kj_per_cm2).

origin: derived by us from RTOFS values
definition: How much RTOFS TCHP at the profile's grid cell departs from its own 1-degree neighbourhood mean.
computation: F[y0, x0] - mean of valid cells in the h = 12 window; from the daily RTOFS field at the nearest grid cell (y0, x0); square window |y - y0| <= h, |x - x0| <= h cells on the native 1/12-degree grid (longitude wraps); valid (finite) cells only, and NaN unless valid cells cover >= 25% of the window. Uses the nearest-cell value, not the interpolated one. Biased near the 26 C edge because sub-threshold cells are excluded rather than counted as zero.

origin: computed by us from RTOFS, with TEOS-10
definition: Steric height of the 1000-2000 dbar layer of the RTOFS water column.
computation: [dyn(0; p_ref=2000) - dyn(0; p_ref=1000)] / g with dyn = gsw.geo_strf_dyn_height at the surface, g = 9.81, from the RTOFS T/S profile interpolated to the Argo point (NaN-safe inverse-distance weighting). Requires the profile to reach 2000 dbar. Available on ~11% of rows (77 processed dates). The ~2% of negative values are all in the Mediterranean (33-44 N, 2-35 E): its deep water is so salty that at 1000-2000 dbar it is denser than the reference water despite being warm, so the specific-volume anomaly and hence the steric height are negative. Physical, not an error.
upstream: RTOFS 3D temperature and salinity profile; TEOS-10 for absolute salinity, Conservative Temperature and dynamic height. RTOFS temperature is potential temperature but is used as in-situ temperature here; see [Known approximation](#known-approximation-potential-vs-in-situ-temperature).

origin: computed by us from RTOFS, with TEOS-10
definition: Maximum buoyancy frequency squared in the upper 200 m of RTOFS.
computation: max of gsw.Nsquared(SA, CT, p, lat) over layer mid-points shallower than 200 m. ~11% coverage.
upstream: RTOFS 3D temperature and salinity profile; TEOS-10 for absolute salinity, Conservative Temperature and N^2. RTOFS temperature is potential temperature but is used as in-situ temperature here; see [Known approximation](#known-approximation-potential-vs-in-situ-temperature).

origin: computed by us from RTOFS, with TEOS-10
definition: Mean buoyancy frequency squared between the surface and RTOFS D26.
computation: mean of gsw.Nsquared over mid-points shallower than model D26. ~11% coverage.
upstream: As model_n2_max_upper200_s2. RTOFS temperature is potential temperature but is used as in-situ temperature here; see [Known approximation](#known-approximation-potential-vs-in-situ-temperature).
